summary: CaptionIQ v3 — template PERSISTENCE retest. The React.StrictMode effect-order race fixed in frontend/src/pages/Studio.jsx (lazy useState initialisers reading from localStorage; separate load useEffect removed) is VERIFIED FIXED on the live preview URL as creator1@test.com. (1) Clicking template-chip-shorts writes {templateId:'shorts',...} to captioniq:style:proj_3bd553caefd9; after page.reload() the value REMAINS 'shorts' (previously reverted to 'modern') and the caption-renderer computed style continues to match Shorts (fontFamily='Anton, sans-serif', fontSize=77.2312px, first-span color=rgb(255,234,0), first-span webkitTextStroke='9.65391px rgb(0, 0, 0)', span_count=4). (2) Same test for Gaming: LS holds 'gaming' after reload and renderer computed style still shows fontFamily='"Russo One", sans-serif' with active-span backgroundColor=rgb(124, 58, 237). Selected-chip ring (border-[#FA5D29] ring-2) also lands on the persisted chip after reload (screenshots confirm the orange outline is on Shorts / Gaming, not Modern). Light regression: (a) renderer span_count=4 out of 12 transcript words — captions still don't cover the video; (b) cycling all 9 template chips fired 0 POSTs to /projects/{id}/transcribe; (c) transcript panel still shows semantic-coloured words (Rahul/Priya as person-yellow, Mumbai/Delhi as location-blue, went/shot as action-green — visible in screenshot); (d) logout redirects to /login. No new bugs found. The bug reported in iteration_3 is now closed.

critical_code_review_comments: Studio.jsx now uses `useState(() => readSaved().templateId)` and `useState(() => readSaved().settings)` with a single save-only useEffect. This is the canonical fix; it survives React.StrictMode's intentional double-invoke because both mounts read the same synchronously-initialised value from localStorage before any save runs. Verified in both directions (write then reload → same value).

Minor nit: `readSaved()` is defined inside the component body, so it re-creates on every render. Not a correctness issue (it only runs inside the lazy initialiser and does no I/O outside), but pulling it out of the component or wrapping with useCallback would silence future lint noise.

Persistence is still per-browser (localStorage). If cross-device continuity is a product goal, the templateId+settings should also be POSTed to the backend on change and hydrated from the project payload on load — the current backend already returns caption_document, so a `caption_style` field would fit naturally.

There are noisy 401 console errors during the initial /dashboard load (previously observed too) — likely the auth/me probe firing before the cookie handshake settles. Harmless but worth suppressing to keep the DevTools console clean.

rca of the issue: Closed. iteration_3 already captured the RCA (StrictMode + save-effect closure clobber). The applied fix — lazy useState initialisers reading from localStorage in Studio.jsx, with the separate load useEffect removed — makes the initial render read the stored templateId synchronously before any save-effect can fire, so the double-mount can no longer overwrite the value with the default. Verified by reading localStorage before/after page.reload() for both templateId='shorts' and templateId='gaming'.
